exercise.name: Meadows Row
library_steps: Stand side-on to the end of a landmine bar, back flat.
Grip the end of the bar overhand, other forearm resting on your knee.
Pull the bar up toward your hip, then lower it slowly.
Finish your reps, then switch sides.
exercise.one_line_summary: Staggered stance side-on to a landmine bar, hips hinged; one hand grips the thick end overhand and rows it to the hip with the elbow flared, the other forearm on the lead knee. Upper back does the most; lats, rear delts and biceps help.

setup.target: Side-on to the bar end, lead foot forward, trunk ~60 deg forward, free forearm on the lead knee.
Overhand on the thick sleeve end.

movement.measure: elbow pulled up and back, flared

muscles.role: Pulls the arm down and back.

muscles.emg: Library secondary; the flared elbow pulls the arm back.
Library secondary; elbow flexor in rows.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: The chest opens to the side as the bar rises.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Momentum instead of the back muscles.

sources.citation: Fenwick CM, Brown SH, McGill SM. 2009. Comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness. J Strength Cond Res.
sources.what_it_gave: Standing bent-over row: large activation across the back from the upper to the lower back; the one-arm row also challenges the trunk against twisting.

sources.citation: Saeterbakken A, Andersen V, Brudeseth A, Lund H, Fimland MS. 2015. The effect of performing bi- and unilateral row exercises on core muscle activation. Int J Sports Med.
sources.what_it_gave: Free-weight bent-over rows one-arm vs two-arm: one-arm rows raised external oblique activity; the back extensors stay active.
